investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-08-04T00:54–01:01Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm (resource quota exhausted or limit reached), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-carrying nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 122–148 seconds across all three checks, the eval runner never received a running VM, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were absent. This is an eval-layer signal of an infrastructure scheduling constraint; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet.

possibleCauses: Most likely — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota exhausted on both eligible nodes: the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector have no remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations, possibly because prior remote-agent pods from earlier eval runs or production workloads were not cleaned up in time.

Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-kata nodes do not match the pod's required node selector, meaning the schedulable pool is effectively limited to 2 nodes; any capacity pressure on those 2 nodes causes total scheduling failure.

Leaked or stuck remote-agent pods from previous eval runs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: the eval runner uses withCleanup (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1883) but if a prior run's cleanup failed, VM slots may remain occupied.

Cluster under-provisioning: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, providing no redundancy; simultaneous eval runs (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime all ran within ~7 minutes of each other) may have contended for the same limited slots.

Transient infrastructure event (node drain, maintenance, or VM provider quota): one or both kata-capable nodes may have been temporarily unavailable or had their extended resource capacity reduced at the time of the run.

investigation.title: published-observability-snapshot Eval Failure: Stale GitHub Actions Snapshot (snapshotAgeMinutes=691, max=300)
investigation.summary: The published observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was last generated 691 minutes ago, exceeding the contract maximum of 300 minutes. This is an eval-level failure localized to the snapshot freshness assertion; all sibling public-website checks (public-observability-page, public-models-page, public-marketing-pages) passed, confirming the web surfaces themselves are reachable and this is not a broad site outage.
investigation.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not run successfully within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot is 691 minutes old at eval time (2026-08-04T01:01:42Z), meaning the last successful publish occurred approximately 11.5 hours prior. The eval contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 asserts snapshotAgeMinutes max 300; the observed value of 691 directly violates this assertion. The root cause is a missed or failed GitHub Actions workflow run that publishes the snapshot, not a failure of the public website itself.

possibleCauses: Most likely: The GitHub Actions workflow that generates and publishes the observability snapshot failed silently or was skipped, leaving the previously published snapshot in place. The snapshot is structurally intact (source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true) but its embedded timestamp is 691 minutes old, indicating the workflow did not complete a fresh publish within the window.

Second: The GitHub Actions workflow was disabled, rate-limited, or its schedule trigger was not honored (e.g., due to repository inactivity policies on GitHub Pages or a cron schedule gap), causing the snapshot to go unrefreshed for over 11 hours.

Third: The workflow ran but failed during the publish step (e.g., a Pages deployment error, a permissions issue, or a build failure), so the old snapshot remained at the published URL without being overwritten.
